svg.title: Autonomous Flight Pilot System Architecture
svg.desc: A layered diagram showing the six core layers of an autonomous flight system, from sensors at the bottom to mission planning at the top, with a safety monitor running alongside all layers.

g.text: GPS, IMU, LiDAR, cameras, pitot tube, barometer, ADS-B receiver
State estimation, obstacle detection, terrain mapping, weather sensing
Path planning, obstacle avoidance, re-routing, AI inference engine
PID controllers, actuator commands, autopilot integration, stability
Ground control link, ATC datalink, satellite comms, failsafe protocols
Flight plan, passenger logic, airspace rules, scheduling, logs

svg.text: Click any layer below to explore it in depth

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Tell me more about Phase 1: the sensor and hardware layer for autonomous flight')
sendPrompt('Tell me more about Phase 2: AI and perception for autonomous flight')
sendPrompt('Tell me more about Phase 3: testing and certification for autonomous aircraft')

svg.text: Similar to autonomous cars, but 3D airspace + zero human override tolerance
Key difference: FAA/DGCA certification required before any real-world flight
Realistic timeline: 5–10 years for full autonomy; simulated MVP in 12–18 months
